what_worked: Consistent emphasis on median over mean and honest acknowledgment of data quality issues.
fix_next: The deck appears built on a different (larger) dataset than the 1,000-row assignment dataset, making most numbers unverifiable and likely wrong.
verdict: Wrong dataset undermines every claim; surface-level insights with decorative visuals.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1/2: Claims 8,782 startups; dataset has 1,000 rows. Slide 2: '59% Use Stripe' = 5,185; reference is 636/1000=63.6%. '36% Country Unknown' stated; reference is 241/1000=24.1%. Slide 4: AI at 1,430 listings; reference is 197. SaaS at 525; reference is 66. AI median MRR $16.90 not verifiable against reference median $503 (30-day revenue). Slide 5: B2B median $15.99 vs B2C $8.37; reference shows median revenue multiples ~2.35x/2.30x, not these absolute values. Slide 6: US 1,657, India 807, France 612, UK 603 — all far from the 1,000-row dataset. Slide 7: Stripe at 5,185 vs reference 636; RevenueCat at 1,236 vs reference 189.

evidence.insight: Observations (power-law, AI paradox, B2B vs B2C) are directionally reasonable but shallow — each slide makes one obvious point without deeper analysis, cross-cuts, or decision-useful recommendations.
evidence.narrative: There is a loose arc from overview → distribution → categories → geography → providers → marketplace → takeaways, but it reads as a topic list rather than building toward a thesis. No synthesis or strategic landing.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 attempts dataset context but uses wrong row count (8,782 vs 1,000). No stated audience, research question, or scope definition. Missingness noted but percentages wrong.
evidence.accuracy: Nearly every quantitative claim is based on what appears to be a different, larger dataset (8,782 rows vs the 1,000-row assignment dataset). Category counts, provider counts, geographic counts, and median values all diverge substantially from reference benchmarks. This is the most serious problem.
evidence.visual: Charts are minimal two-bar comparisons that add little beyond the text. Decorative AI-generated imagery (slide 1 dashboard, slide 6 fantasy map, slide 8 storefront illustration) is visually noisy and unrelated to the data. Gamma template is repetitive. No annotations, no multi-variable charts.
evidence.ai_slop: Slide 1 features a generic neon dashboard image unrelated to the dataset. Slide 6 uses a stylized fantasy-style world map. Slide 8 uses an AI-generated storefront illustration. All are decorative filler with no analytical value. Template structure is cookie-cutter Gamma output.
